title: Fix autonomy failure infrastructure classification
summary: Stopped autonomy health from classifying source-media encode failure records as infrastructure failures merely because their structured evidence contains fields such as source_path, artifact_path, reproduction_path, or repro_path.
reason: The live readiness blocker was reported as repeated network/share/disk/copy/publish failures, but internal state showed 10 SOURCE_MEDIA_STREAM_UNSUPPORTED NVENC encode failures from Ascendance of a Bookworm S03. The classifier searched field names and values together, so the word path in evidence keys made ordinary source-media failure markers trip the infrastructure launch gate.
behavior_before: Failure infrastructure detection searched all scalar key/value pairs together. Structured field names such as source_path and repro_path could make unrelated source-media encode failures count as network/share/disk/copy/publish infrastructure failures and block new launches.
behavior_after: Failure infrastructure detection only searches selected evidence values such as reason, error_code, operation, classification, operator_action, and suggested_action. Source/artifact/repro path field names no longer trigger infrastructure classification, while true network-share/publish failures still block after the repeated-failure threshold.
manual_validation: apps/desktop/runtime/Python/python.exe -m mediapipeline.tools.autonomy_health_gate --paths-json <live E:\Videos\Scratch payload> - passed (exit 0; overall=review; can_start_new_work=True; blocked_count=0; failure_artifacts=20; infrastructure_count=0)
rollback_plan: Revert src/mediapipeline/core/diagnostics/autonomy_health.py and tests/python/desktop/test_autonomy_health.py, refresh the two generated summaries, and delete this change packet. Do not clear runtime failure markers or mutate source media as part of rollback.
notes:
Constrain infrastructure failure classification to evidence values instead of structured path field names.
Add regressions for source-media path fields versus true network-share failures.
